blocks.text: Managing tabs as an e-commerce merchandiser

Your day involves jumping from a Google Sheet for inventory to a Shopify product page. You likely have twenty tabs open at once. This creates what many call channel sprawl. It slows your Mac and your brain. Start by grouping your tabs. Right click on any tab in Chrome and select Add tab to new group. You can color code these for different tasks. Use one group for analytics and another for content updates. This keeps your visual space clean.
Using Chrome profiles for store separation

If you manage multiple store accounts, do not mix them in one profile. Use the profile switcher in Chrome. Click your profile icon at the top right, then click Add. This creates a separate instance of Chrome. Each profile keeps its own cookies, logins, and history. You will not accidentally post a social update to the wrong brand account. It is the safest way to manage multiple client stores on one Mac.

Lazur helps you when you get stuck in a complex web interface. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about a setting you cannot find. If you are looking at a dense dashboard, ask Lazur where the export button is. It will draw a circle around it. You do not need to hunt through menus. This saves seconds every time you perform a repetitive task. Over a week, these seconds add up to hours of saved time.
Keyboard shortcuts for Chrome on Mac

items: ⌘ + L: Jump to the address bar immediately.
⌘ + Option + Right Arrow: Move to the next tab.
⌘ + W: Close the current tab quickly.
⌘ + Shift + T: Reopen the last closed tab if you make a mistake.

blocks.text: Merchandising is mostly data work. You often need to count unique SKUs or clean up product lists. If you are not sure how to use a formula, ask Lazur to explain it. You can say, how do I count unique items in this column. Lazur explains the formula. You then type it into your sheet. This is faster than searching through help forums for a simple answer.

E-commerce dashboards are heavy. They run many scripts and trackers. If Chrome feels slow, check your extensions. Go to Chrome > Settings > Extensions. Remove anything you do not use daily. Extensions are a common source of browser instability. If a page refuses to load, try clearing the cache for that specific site first. You do not need to clear your entire history. Use the site settings menu to target the problem.

blocks.text: How to get help with Lazur

Lazur is a voice assistant that sits in your Mac notch. It does not click things for you. It helps you find the right path. When you are confused by a new tool, ask Lazur to guide you. It will walk you through the steps one by one. It waits for you to perform each click. This is helpful when you are learning a new vendor portal or inventory system.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Shopify products?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It guides you so you can do the work yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur is currently built only for macOS. Windows support is planned for the future.

faq.question: Is my screen data private?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut. The data is not stored or used to train AI models.

faq.question: How do I speed up Chrome on my Mac?
faq.answer: Remove unused extensions, clear cache for problematic sites, and use separate profiles for different tasks.
